# Machine Learning Engineer
Manchester, UK · Full-time
Apply
About Precica
## Who we are.
Precica (precica.ai) is a deep-tech spinout of the University of Manchester, backed by Northern Gritstone and Deeptech Labs. Our product, pdata, compresses data by orders of magnitude whilst keeping it directly queryable — with applications in analytics, ML, querying, and forecasting. We're running live pilots in electricity markets and expanding into unstructured data (video, logs, sensor streams). Precica is an early-stage company with a small founding team, tackling one of the defining infrastructure problems of the coming decade: the cost, energy, and carbon footprint of dark data.
The Role
## What you'll do.
We're seeking a Machine Learning Engineer with a focus on neural and learned data compression. The role involves designing, implementing, and optimising compression models that underpin pdata's core engine.
Responsibilities include developing and benchmarking compression pipelines for structured and unstructured data, performing statistical evaluation of rate–distortion and query-accuracy trade-offs, and deploying models into production and pilot environments.
You will work directly with the founding team to translate research advances into scalable product capability, maintain code quality and reproducibility, and contribute to technical documentation and white papers.
As one of the first technical hires, you will have unusual scope to shape the company's technical direction. Responsibility at Precica grows with contribution and with the company itself — those who build the core of the product will be well placed to lead as we scale.
Requirements
## What we're looking for.
Essential
* Strong foundation in Computer Science: data structures, algorithms, and software engineering principles.
* Applied expertise in machine learning, with hands-on experience building and tuning models on real-world data.
* In-depth understanding of neural architectures relevant to compression and representation learning.
* Proficiency in statistics, probability, and experimental design for rigorous model evaluation.
* Fluency in Python and modern ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) and adaptability to work across frameworks.
* Experience with large datasets, data pipelines, and version control (Git).
* Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly and document work thoroughly.
* Degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field.
Desirable
* Direct experience with neural or learned compression: quantisation-aware training, rate–distortion optimisation, or learned transforms.
* Postgraduate degree or research experience in machine learning, information theory, signal processing, or data compression.
* Background in low-rank or structured representations (e.g. tensor decompositions, sketching, dimensionality reduction).
* Experience with time-series modelling and forecasting, particularly in energy or industrial settings.
* Familiarity with embedding-based retrieval and video/image representation learning (e.g. CLIP-style models, vector search).
* Performance engineering skills: C++, CUDA, or optimisation of inference pipelines for throughput and memory.
* Experience deploying models to production (MLOps, containerisation, CI/CD) and with cloud or HPC environments.
* Publications, open-source contributions, or patents in a relevant area.
Logistics
## A few practical details.
* Minimum education: Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
* Required field of study: Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field relevant to the role.
* Minimum years of experience: This is an entry-level role — we weigh demonstrated ability and relevant project or research experience over years on paper.
* Location-based hybrid policy: Precica is based in Manchester, UK. This role is hybrid — specific in-office expectations will be confirmed during the interview process.
* Visa sponsorship: We do not currently sponsor visas — we don't hold a sponsorship licence. You must already have the right to work in the UK to apply for this role.
We encourage you to apply even if you don't believe you meet every single qualification listed. Not all strong candidates tick every box, and research shows that people from underrepresented groups are especially prone to underestimating their own fit — so please don't rule yourself out prematurely. Problems like the one we're solving benefit from a wide range of perspectives, and we're building Precica with that in mind.
Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Precica recruiters only contact you from @precica.ai email addresses — be cautious of emails from other domains claiming to represent us. Legitimate Precica recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links — get in touch with us directly at contact@precica.ai to confirm.

About Prevail Partners
Prevail Partners is a leading British intelligence, security and operational support company. We help governments, NGOs and commercial organisations operate safely and effectively in some of the world's most complex environments by combining intelligence, technology and operational expertise. Our teams deliver actionable insight that helps clients manage risk, make informed decisions and achieve meaningful operational impact where it matters most. Our shared mission is to deliver unrelenting excellence in everything we do, underpinned by integrity, curiosity, accountability and care. About the Role
We are seeking a Junior Software Engineer (Data) to join our Platform & System Operations (PSO) team on a permanent basis.
Prevail’s PSO team builds the tools and platforms of our technology landscape, used day to day by the intelligence analysts behind our client investigations. Today these solutions are highly specialised and application-specific, but they share the same backend core: Databricks, AWS and Python, with React on the frontend where needed. We're bringing these tools together into a single, consolidated intelligence platform, and this role will play a part in that evolution.
Reporting to the Software Team Lead , the Junior Software Engineer (Data) will build and ship solutions to a wide range of problems, working with analysts and business development to decide what to build, what to extend and where an existing tool will do the job better. We are looking for a curious and proactive individual who takes ownership of their work, builds strong relationships with others, stays organised under competing priorities, and is eager to learn and grow. The ideal candidate is comfortable seeking support when needed and demonstrates professionalism and discretion when handling sensitive information. It’s a great opportunity for someone early in their career who is technically curious, enjoys solving practical problems, and wants to build real delivery and engineering experience while working alongside senior engineers and the rest of the team.
Given the sensitive nature of the data our tools hold, this role is subject to background screening, and you will need to be eligible for UK security clearance.
Key Responsibilities:
Build, test and release features and fixes across our internal tools and platforms, taking your own work through to production with review from senior colleagues.
Write and maintain Python and SQL across our data pipelines, backend services and the queries that power our tools, with code review from senior colleagues.
Work closely with intelligence analysts to understand the problems they're trying to solve, translate these into scoped pieces of work, and turn their feedback into improvements you deliver, escalating the larger items to engineers and product owners.
Deepen your working knowledge of Databricks, AWS, Python and React, taking on more of the stack as you develop.
Help evaluate and integrate third-party tools where buying beats building, working with analysts and business development to test the options and wire the chosen tool into our environment.
Support analysts day to day, triaging issues and escalating technical problems where needed.
Document solutions, workflows and known issues clearly, contributing to a growing knowledge base for the team.
Maintain high standards of data security and information handling given the sensitive nature of the intelligence and client data our tools support.
Essential Skills and Experience: Hands-on coding experience in Python and SQL, whether from a degree, personal projects, internships or previous roles, and the appetite to pick up cloud and data platforms quickly.
Familiarity with version control (Git) and a willingness to work to the team's review, testing and documentation standards.
A degree in a relevant subject (e.g. computer science, data, engineering, or a related technical or analytical discipline), or equivalent practical experience.
Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down a user's problem and think through practical, workable solutions.
Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to testing, documenting and troubleshooting.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical users and vice versa.
Comfortable working directly with end users, building relationships and gathering requirements through conversation.
Desirable Skills and Experience:
Exposure to Databricks, Spark, AWS or React, whether through study, personal projects or previous roles.
Previous experience as a software engineer, data engineering or analytics role, including internships and placements.
Experience working in an agile or fast-paced software development environment.
An interest in or awareness of the intelligence, OSINT, security or investigations space.
Experience producing clear technical documentation and user guides.

job_description:
Job Description
What is the opportunity?
You will be responsible for making sure every price, security, fund, broker, and benchmark record we rely on is accurate, complete, and on time. This data underpins trading, NAV calculations, client reporting, and regulatory filings, so the quality bar is high and the work is genuinely consequential.
This is as much a people-leadership role as a technical one. The team is capable and fully staffed having recently had some turnover. Your first and most important job is to bring them together: to help talented people across two locations gel into a close, connected team with a shared sense of purpose and a common way of working. From that foundation, you'll build on the strong operational base already in place, driving the operational excellence, process improvement, and governance that the role also demands.
Should you be shortlisted, do please let us know if you have any specific requirements for the interview.
This is a permanent, full-time role and requires 4 days in the office at our 100 Bishopsgate, London office.
What will you do?
Bring the team together
Help a group of Senior Data Analysts and Data Analysts, across London and Stamford, grow into a close-knit team with a shared identity, clear norms, and genuine trust
Build the connections that let knowledge flow both ways, so everyone feels part of one group
Keep both locations equally connected and visible, one team, two desks, with London and Stamford working as genuine partners
Sustain and strengthen the everyday rhythm that keeps a team close: regular 1:1s, clear priorities, shared handovers, and consistent follow-through
Coach and develop each person, run real career conversations and performance reviews, and build a collaborative, continuous-improvement culture
Own pricing and reference data operations
Oversee daily pricing operations for bonds, derivatives, equities, and loans across the IVP Price Master and market data platforms (Bloomberg, Pricing Direct, ICE Data Services, Refinitiv, S&P)
Ensure timely, accurate maintenance of security, fund, broker, benchmark, and reference data across key systems (IVP Security Master, SimCorp Dimension, Charles River, Wall Street Office)
Monitor and resolve escalated pricing and reference data issues, and act as the primary escalation point for the function
Maintain and improve data quality standards and controls, and provide input on tooling, systems, and vendor services
Assign and balance workload so capacity matches business demand, and protects the team from unmanaged, ill-sequenced urgency
Drive improvement and manage risk
Lead process improvement and automation initiatives using Python, SQL, and generative AI
Identify and implement control enhancements that reduce operational and regulatory risk
Lead system upgrade projects and assess the downstream impact of data and process changes
Maintain team documentation, procedures, and best practices
Ensure compliance with valuation policies and regulatory requirements, and coordinate audit and regulatory responses related to pricing and reference data
Manage stakeholders and communication
Build strong working relationships across Investment Desks, Operations, Client Reporting, Fund Accounting, Risk/Performance & Attribution, and IT Development
Coordinate with internal teams on new initiatives to ensure data flows and translations stay correct
Provide regular, clear updates and management reporting to senior leadership
What do you need to succeed?
Must-have

About Reap
Reap is a global financial technology company headquartered in Hong Kong with employees across multiple countries. We enable financial connectivity and access for businesses worldwide by combining traditional finance with stablecoins for efficient money movement.
Through our stablecoin-powered corporate cards, payments, and expense management tools, we streamline financial operations and help businesses scale. Our APIs enable businesses to integrate stablecoin-enabled finance into their own products and services—from issuing Visa cards to facilitating cross-border payments.
Backed by leading investors including Acorn Pacific, Index Ventures and HashKey Capital, Reap is building the future of borderless, stablecoin-enabled finance.
Why Reap?
Payments are one of the Business Account's core products and the engine of money movement across the platform. Whether our customers are paying vendors and suppliers globally or receiving funds from their own clients, Payments provide the rails and the workflows that connect every financial activity they run with us. We are looking for someone to take full ownership of this product and carry it forward.
This is a chance to own a high-usage, high-stakes product end-to-end: the customer experience, the payment flows underneath it, the compliance and operational realities that shape them, and the roadmap that decides what comes next. You will set the direction, decide what matters most, and keep the experience feeling simple even as the complexity grows across markets, currencies, and entities.
The mandate here is broad on purpose. Our embedded finance team owns the core infrastructure, while you own the user experience and the distribution, and you carry real influence over where their roadmap goes. You will have direct access to leadership, room to shape strategy, and the space to make decisions that visibly move the product forward. If you want to own a meaningful product surface rather than a narrow slice of one, and you treat AI tools as part of your everyday toolkit, this is a strong fit.
Your Mission Awaits
Own Payments end-to-end: Take full responsibility for Payments as a product, from strategy and discovery through delivery, iteration, and the operational follow-through that keeps payments moving. You define where the product goes and why, and you make sure it gets there.
Set direction and prioritize: Build a clear point of view on what the product needs, decide what to do now versus later, and keep the roadmap focused on what genuinely matters for customers and for the business.
Turn payment complexity into a clear experience: Work closely with engineering and design to translate onboarding, KYB and KYC, payee setup, approval chains, and multi-currency settlement into journeys that feel simple, reliable, and trustworthy for business customers.
Partner with embedded finance on the rails: They own the core infrastructure and you own the experience and distribution on top of it, so a large part of this role is influencing their roadmap and making sure the flows work seamlessly across entities, currencies, and geographies.
Keep the product compliant and reliable as it scales: Work with legal, compliance, risk, and our banking partners so the product stays sound against regional and global regulation, and balance speed with the rigor that payments demand.
Measure what matters: Define and track the success metrics for the product, including adoption, retention, payment volume, and speed of payment, and use them to stay honest about what is and is not working.
Partner across the organization: Work fluidly with engineering, design, compliance, operations, finance, and go-to-market teams to ship well and to keep the product healthy as it grows.
Your Superpowers
7 to 10 years of product management experience, with at least 5 years in fintech, payments, or SaaS platforms, including products you carried end-to-end rather than managed as a single feature.
Proven track record launching and scaling complex payment products, such as cross-border, B2B, treasury or payment rails, and funding in and out.
Direct experience with stablecoins, blockchain payment rails, or digital asset infrastructure. This one is required, not a nice to have.
Strong grasp of multi-currency and multi-entity payment operations, and of what breaks when either of those scales.
Technical fluency: you do not need to code, but you do need to speak payments and engineering credibly with the teams building the rails.
Obsession with great user experience, with a track record of simplifying complex financial workflows without losing the rigor underneath.
Analytical and strategic mindset, comfortable balancing a long-term view with rapid iteration in a fast-moving environment.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence technical and business stakeholders and to earn trust through clarity and results rather than authority.
Nice to Have
Familiarity with card-to-bank payments, invoice financing, or FX settlement.
Experience in early-stage startups or scaling organizations, ideally across multiple geographies.
Knowledge of regional payment ecosystems, particularly APAC or LatAm, and the ability to navigate fragmented rails.
Why You'll Love it Here
A high-impact role in a rapidly growing fintech startup
Flexible hybrid work environment with a global, collaborative team
Insurance coverage after probation
Reap Card stipend
Use of AI tools at work, and the space to learn, experiment, and grow with them
A culture of innovation, inclusion, and continuous learning

## Job Description
**About Schroders**
We’re a global investment manager. We help institutions, intermediaries and individuals around the world invest money to meet their goals, fulfil their ambitions, and prepare for the future.
We have around 6,000 people on six continents. And we’ve been around for over 200 years, but keep adapting as society and technology changes. What doesn’t change is our commitment to helping our clients, and society, prosper.
**The base**
We moved into our new HQ in the City of London in 2018. We’re close to our clients, in the heart of the UK’s financial centre and we have everything we need to work flexibly.
**The team**
The Group-level 1st Line Risk & Controls team is the central hub for first-line control excellence, frameworks, standards and strategic delivery across Schroders. It is part of the Finance team and operates within a hub-and-spoke model, working with embedded Business Control Officers across the group.
The team defines first-line standards, drives consistency, consolidates MI, supports governance, provides targeted control advisory support, and helps move the control environment from reactive issue management to proactive risk identification, control effectiveness and automation-enabled monitoring. It is at the center of the hub-and-spoke model, focusing on frameworks, standards, RCA / RCSA consistency, material controls, MI, escalation, evidence expectations and risk-based testing, in addition to Finance-specific control priorities including ISAE 3402 support, operational resilience reporting, third-party risk management, operational due diligence, Finance transformation control uplift and CFO / COO governance reporting.
**The role**
Reporting to the Group Head of Controls, the Senior Manager will be a senior delivery lead responsible for developing, embedding and operationalising first-line control frameworks, standards, MI, issue/risk event management and testing activity across the Group, including Finance. The role will work closely with Business Control Officers across Finance, Public Markets, Schroders Capital, Wealth Management, Client Group, Technology / InfoSec and the Global Operating Platform, as well as with Finance leadership, Group Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit, Group COO stakeholders and senior business stakeholders.
This role is suited to an experienced risk and control professional who can combine technical control expertise, practical business judgement, constructive challenge and strong stakeholder management, and who can translate Finance control priorities into pragmatic operating standards, governance reporting and senior management insight.
**What you'll do**
**Frameworks, standards and operating model**
* Support the Group Head of Controls in developing, maintaining and embedding first-line control frameworks, standards and minimum expectations across the group.
* Translate Group Risk methodology, policy and requirements into practical first-line standards for control design, evidence, MI, escalations, testing and issue management.
* Help operationalise the hub-and-spoke model by aligning embedded Business Control Officers to common ways of working while preserving local business ownership.
* Define and maintain guidance, templates and standards that support consistent execution across business areas.
* Identify opportunities to simplify, standardise and improve first-line control processes, data quality and reporting.
* Lead the application of Finance-specific control standards across key Finance processes, including financial control, reporting, cost processes, supplier lifecycle controls, management information and Finance transformation activity.
**RCA / RCSA and material controls**
* Support consistent RCA / RCSA execution across business areas, working closely with embedded Business Control Officers and Group Risk.
* Provide first-line quality review and challenge over risk identification, control mapping, ratings, actions and escalation.
* Support the development and implementation of material control standards, evidence expectations and control inventory requirements.
* Identify control gaps, thematic weaknesses and opportunities to improve the design and operation of key controls.
* Ensure Finance risks, controls, actions and evidence expectations are consistently captured through RCA / RCSA and material control activity, with outputs capable of senior management and governance review.
**Risk-based testing and control improvement**
* Develop and help deliver a risk-based testing approach focused initially on the firm’s most material risks and controls.
* Support the definition of annual testing expectations, including what should be tested, by whom, how frequently and to what evidence standard.
* Lead or support thematic control reviews where risks are material, cross-cutting or recurring.
* Work with business areas to ensure testing outcomes are clearly documented, reported and remediated.
* Support the future development of automated controls testing and continuous control monitoring.
* Lead Finance-specific assurance and control activities, including ISAE 3402 engagement support, operational resilience reporting, third-party risk management, operational due diligence and control uplift linked to Finance transformation initiatives.
**MI, governance and escalation**
* Develop consistent first-line Group-level MI, dashboards, risk insights and governance reporting for senior management forums.
* Consolidate and analyse control themes, risk events, issues, audit findings, RCA outputs, testing results and remediation progress.
* Prepare high-quality reporting and briefing materials for senior stakeholders and relevant governance forums.
* Define escalation thresholds and support escalation of material or unresolved control matters.
* Develop and deliver Finance and Group-level governance reporting, including risk and control inputs for Group CFO / Group COO materials, Operating Committee activity, Group Risk Committee and Board Audit and Risk Committee reporting where required.
**Stakeholder management and culture**
* Build strong relationships with embedded Business Control Officers, business leadership, Group Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and other assurance functions.
* Provide coaching, guidance and constructive challenge to first-line stakeholders on control responsibilities, evidence standards, testing and issue management.
* Promote a strong risk awareness culture, accountability and consistent ways of working across the First Line.
* Support capability development and sharing of best practice across business areas.
* Work with Finance leadership and embedded control officers to promote clear ownership of Finance risks and controls, practical escalation routes and proportionate control design across Finance processes and change activity.
**The knowledge, experience and qualifications you need**
* Significant experience in operational risk, controls, assurance, audit, compliance, finance controls or first-line risk management within financial services.
* Strong understanding of Finance processes and controls, including financial reporting, management reporting, supplier payments, reconciliations, audit actions, cost processes, supplier lifecycle controls and Finance governance.
* Strong understanding of first-line risk and control frameworks, RCA / RCSA, control design, control testing, issue management and risk reporting.

* Experience leading or supporting risk-based testing, thematic reviews or control assurance activity.
* Strong analytical capability with the ability to interpret risk and control data and translate it into actionable senior management insight.
* Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, including the ability to challenge constructively and operate across senior business, risk, compliance and audit stakeholders.

* Experience in managing direct reports, providing guidance, training, and leadership.

* Run tests outside of Creator Connections in the US and through central affiliate go-to-market in your region.
* Draw clear implications from the results and write them into our Centre of Excellence playbook.
* Identify, contact and onboard creators and affiliate partners in market.
* Track performance by format, creator and category, and build a defensible view of what converts.
* Work with Sales and Digital Marketing to make sure affiliate traffic lands on pages that are ready to convert.

* Genuinely interested in creators, content and how people are persuaded to buy online.
* Analytical and comfortable working with data to identify trends and support decision making.
* A confident communicator who can turn complex information into something clear and actionable.

## The Role & Responsibilities
Platform is a new and deliberate idea at Shawbrook. Rather than every part of the bank solving the same foundational problems again and again, we are building shared platform services, the capabilities that everything else is built on. Done well, these foundations let our lending, mortgages, deposits and servicing value streams move faster, more safely, and at lower cost.
This role does two things at once. It **leads delivery** across four platform teams, and it ***shapes the platform model itself,*** how platform teams work, how the verticals consume them, and what good looks like for a foundational service. This is not a role that inherits a finished operating model. It is a role that helps define one.
**Key Responsibilities**
**The teams you will lead** - You will be accountable for the delivery outcomes of four platform teams:
**Vault**
Core banking on Thought Machine — the ledger and product engine the bank is migrating onto. Buy to Let is already live, with the wider migration underway.
**Payments**
The payments platform — moving money safely, reliably and at scale on behalf of every customer-facing product.
**Customer**
The shared customer capability — a single, consistent view of the customer that the verticals build on.
**Accounts**
The shared accounts capability — the foundational account services the rest of the bank consumes.
*Together these are the foundations of the bank. Your job is to make them dependable, reusable and genuinely enabling — so the value streams can move faster because the platform is solid beneath them.*
**What you will own**
* **Shaping the platform way of working** — help define what platform means at Shawbrook: the operating model, how teams run as platforms rather than projects, and the standards for a foundational service. This is the differentiator of the role.
* **Platform as an enabler** — treat the verticals as your customers. Make the platform something they choose to build on because it makes them faster and safer, not slower.
* **End to end delivery outcomes** across Vault, Payments, Customer and Accounts — aligning delivery to business and customer value.
* **The domain roadmap** — balancing value, risk and capacity across four teams, and managing the interdependencies between them and the verticals that rely on them.
* **The SteerCo narrative and its quality** — a clear, honest platform story covering RAYG status, risks, financials and decisions, with no surprises. Any non green status carries a credible path to green with dates.
* **Domain level risk** — mitigation, escalation and governance proportionate to the foundational, regulated services you run, including key person, third party and route to live environment risk.
* **The delivery budget** — accurate forecasting within tolerance and disciplined management of vendor and partner performance (for example Thought Machine and other platform partners).
* **Your people** — line managing Senior Delivery Managers, building capability and succession depth, and owning engagement, psychological safety and retention as core deliverables.
* **The AI agenda for the domain** — championing adoption to lift delivery speed, predictability and quality.
## The Person
**Skills and experience**
* Substantial delivery leadership experience owning outcomes across a domain, platform, value stream or large portfolio in financial services.
* A platform mindset — you think in terms of reusable, foundational capabilities and treating internal teams as customers, and you are energised by shaping a model rather than inheriting one.
* Deep understanding of agile, lean and product centric delivery within a regulated environment, including governance, risk and audit expectations.
* Proven ownership of a delivery budget, forecasting and vendor performance at domain scale.
* Experience line managing and developing senior delivery professionals, and building team capability and culture.
* Credible at SteerCo and with senior Product and Engineering leaders; able to own a domain narrative and influence prioritisation.

* Trust over control.

* Outcomes over tasks.

**About you**

Lead Product Designer - Cortex
📍 Manchester (Hybrid, up to 4 days WFH)
💰 Competitive salary, dependent on experience
Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to transform the experience of buying, selling, renting and letting property, elevating UK estate agencies through world-class technology.
Cortex is an exciting new product that brings agentic AI into Street and Spectre, taking on the busywork so agents can focus on winning instructions and building relationships. It's early, moving fast, and will ultimately touch every part of the product suite. We're looking for a Lead Product Designer to shape what agentic UX looks like across all of it.
We want someone who is genuinely excited by agentic AI, past needing to be told what's worth working on, and ready to help define a product category that doesn't have a playbook yet - working closely with senior stakeholders across the business.
If you look at most UX job ads, you see a laundry list of requirements. We prefer to tell you how we actually operate so you can decide if this is the right environment for you.
At Street Group, design is a strategic seat. You'll drive direction alongside product and engineering, not respond to them.
Our users rely on us to run their businesses, so they love talking to us. You can spin up a call and validate a prototype instantly. We don't guess; we ask.
We move at pace, including on strategic work. Strategy isn't a separate, slower track here - we test it by shipping.
Here's what you can expect to be working on
Shape the UX of agentic AI across Street and Spectre - deciding which agency workflows agents should own, then designing how that actually feels and builds trust for the user.
Design across the whole suite, not one domain - valuation, prospecting, marketing, enquiry handling, sales progression, property management. You'll hold a huge amount of context.
Define the patterns for a new category. There's no established playbook for agentic UX in property - you'll set it.
Set the craft bar through your own output. The work you ship is the reference point for what good looks like.
Prototype, test and ship at pace - getting working prototypes in front of real agents and iterating fast.
You should apply if:
You've built or shaped agentic AI, not just used AI tools - multi-step, tool-using agents you've designed, prototyped or shipped. You understand how they work and where they break.
You've got a well-formed point of view on agentic UX - how you design for systems that don't always behave the same way, how you build in trust, transparency and control, and when to keep a human in the loop.
You stay current. This field moves monthly and you keep on top of it.
You're energised by an undefined problem space and bring the case for what's worth doing, rather than waiting for a brief.
You're commercially fluent - you make design trade-offs informed by how the product performs, not just user preference. You define success before you ship and read the result after.
You probably shouldn't apply if:
Your AI experience is limited to speeding up your own workflow. This role is about designing AI into the product, and that gap will show quickly.
You're looking for the next pay band up from Senior with broadly similar expectations. This is not a "Senior+" role - it expects materially more scope, autonomy and judgment.
You need a well-defined problem before you can start. Cortex is still taking shape, and that won't change soon.
You expect to be handed a roadmap. Here, you help write it.
A bit about you
AI & agentic depth: Non-negotiable, and the first thing we'll screen for. Current, hands-on knowledge of agentic AI, with real examples of what you've built or shaped.
Craft: Lead-level UX and product design. Your work is exemplary and you can articulate it clearly enough to teach.
Breadth: Comfortable operating across the whole product suite and holding a lot of context at once, not going deep on a single domain.
Ambiguity: You do your best work when the problem isn't yet defined.
Cross-functional: A peer at the table with product and engineering, partnering closely with a good PM without treading on each other's toes.
Technical fluency: Being hands-on enough to prototype with code is a real advantage here, given how close design sits to how these systems work. It's a plus, not a hard requirement.
Experience: Typically this comes with around 8+ years in product/UX design at senior IC level - but we care more about evidence you can operate at Lead altitude than the exact number, especially given how new agentic AI is. SaaS or complex product experience is helpful; property experience isn't required.
Research has shown that women tend to rule themselves out of applying for jobs unless they meet 100% of the requirements. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application.

# Research Engineer
London (expect 5 days in office)Full-time
## About us
Telluvian is a London-based, VC-backed pre-seed startup. We use mechanistic interpretability, our understanding of what's happening inside neural networks, to make AI cheaper and more secure. Learn more at telluvian.ai.
## The role
We're looking for a generalist ML researcher to take on the interpretability questions we're facing and turn what we learn into things we can build. Prior interpretability experience isn't required, but more general experience with ML is.
Due to the nature of interpretability, this involves a lot of very open-ended work where there is no one right answer. In some cases you may be handed a research direction, but in many cases you will be able to decide on the direction yourself.
You'll need to be a competent engineer to do this research, but only in the ways that serve it. Confident Python is the bar; frontend skills aren't expected.
You'll join a team of fewer than ten people. Your research will form a key part of our product pipeline.
This is a full time position with flexible working hours. We ask that you're in person in the London office minimum four days a week.
Start date is flexible but our target date is early September.
## What you'll do
* Research interpretability questions, including choosing which ones are worth asking. You'll set your own directions as often as you're given them.

At Tide, we help SMEs save time and money in the running of their businesses by not only offering business accounts and related banking services, but also a comprehensive set of highly usable and connected administrative solutions, from invoicing to accounting.
Tide is transforming the small business banking market and now supports over 2 million members globally across the UK, India, Germany and France.

**Tide facts:**
* Tide is available for UK, Indian, German and French SMEs
* Over 2 million members: 900,000 UK and 1,100,000 in India and growing rapidly
* Over $300 million raised in funding
* Over 2,800 Tideans globally
* Recognised with Great Place to Work certification three years in a row, and among India’s Top 50 Best Workplaces in Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance in 2026
* We have offices in Central London, with a member support and technology centre in Sofia, Bulgaria, technology centres in Serbia, Romania, Lithuania and Hyderabad and offices in Gurugram, New Delhi, Berlin, Paris and Luxembourg
### ABOUT THE TEAM:
We are pleased to have a dynamic, forward-thinking group of professionals, deeply committed to supporting Tide in its growth while maintaining the highest standards of regulatory compliance and risk management. We have great cross-collaboration both within and outside the team and we pride ourselves on our team culture, ways of working and the support we provide to each other and to the business.
If joining the Compliance Team, you will be part of a supportive and knowledgeable group, with opportunities to work on complex, high-impact projects that contribute directly to Tide's success and growth. You'll be encouraged to bring new ideas, challenge the status quo, and take ownership of key compliance initiatives.
**ABOUT THE ROLE:**
As Regulatory Risk & Compliance Manager - UK, you will play a vital role in ensuring Tide complies with the evolving regulatory requirements set by the FCA and other UK regulators, with particular ownership of Tide's e-money and payments compliance. You will advise the business on what it can and cannot do under Tide's e-money permission, identify, assess, and mitigate regulatory risk, and ensure that Tide's compliance frameworks are embedded across the business.
You will sit alongside two other UK Compliance colleagues, reporting directly to the Global Director of Compliance, and will provide regulatory compliance support more broadly across the business as needed.
Working closely with teams across the organization, including Product, Member Operations, Payments, Marketing, Legal and Finance, you will provide expert advice on regulatory developments, lead compliance initiatives, and integrate regulatory requirements into our day-to-day operations.
As the subject matter expert on e-money and payments regulation, you'll help to steer decisions, impact strategies and support the rest of the team and business. At Tide, you'll be able to work in a fast-paced environment, with cross-team exposure, inquisitive freedom and the ability to impact how Tide conducts its business.
**As Regulatory Risk & Compliance Manager you will:**
* Advise on the scope of Tide's e-money permission, and lead compliance with the Electronic Money Regulations 2011 and Payment Services Regulations 2017, including related regulatory submissions and notifications.
* Lead engagement on FCA correspondence, submissions, inspections, and thematic reviews.

## **Grow with Treefera**
We are a first-mile intelligence platform, delivering granular visibility into the point of origin in global ag & soft commodity supply chains - where risk, cost, performance and exposure are set.
You’ll join a global, cross-functional team that values rigour, curiosity and working close to real-world challenges. Whether your focus is AI, climate, product or operations, you’ll have space to contribute meaningfully and make an impact from day one.
If you’re excited by complex problems and want to help reshape how nature is valued in real-world decision-making, we’d love to hear from you.
### **Role overview**
You will take ownership of the Market Intelligence and signals Treefera delivers. You'll turn our automatically generated monthly insights into a definitive Treefera view that traders act on, and call the market events worth publishing between cycles. You will monitor your assigned markets and, as you settle into the role, become a recognised voice for Treefera among commodity analysts and at industry events.
### **Who you are**
* You bring deep, practical knowledge of commodity markets — how prices move, and how supply & demand play out across regions and seasons.
* You have the editorial judgement to take a draft and turn it into a piece that carries a clear point of view, and the confidence to put your name to it.
* You write for the physical market — you know how traders and buyers actually read, and you can spot language that won't land with them.
* You can represent your analysis externally — building relationships with analysts and putting a view across at events and briefings.
* You work without a fixed roadmap, calling the market events worth publishing as they happen and setting your own priorities as demand shifts.
**Desirable requirements (if applicable):**
* Experience at a price-reporting agency, commodity desk, or market publication — the outlooks and commentary the market actually reads.
* A track record of external presence — quoted commentary, conference speaking, or an existing network among commodity analysts.
* Familiarity with AI-assisted drafting and research workflows, and a clear sense of where human judgement has to override them.
### **What the job involves**
* **Own the monthly market insight** — review, sharpen and sign off the monthly sentiment papers across our full dataset portfolio (12 a month today, scaling towards 18) so each one reflects a considered Treefera view on supply, demand and the market and political factors that move prices.
* **Hold the market voice** — make sure what we publish reads the way the physical market reads, catching terminology and framing that won't land with traders and buyers.
* **Monitor the markets proactively** — track the commodities we cover and flag significant events, from weather to official crop estimates, that are worth communicating to clients.
* **Be a Treefera voice in the market** — as your cadence establishes, build relationships with commodity analysts and represent our view at events and briefings.
* **Partner with Product Marketing** — turn your market views into newsletters, bulletins and campaigns, judging when an event is worth publishing, and maintaining editorial standards alongside them.
* **Work closely with the Science & AI team** — understand what our models are telling us so the view you publish is grounded in what the data actually shows.
### **What success looks like**
In your first 30 days you'll be close to the commodities we model, across how our insights come together, and mapping the analysts who cover our markets. By 60 days you're signing off your first full monthly cycle with a clear Treefera view running through it. By 90 days you've published your first proactive event callout between cycles and made your first analyst introductions. By six months the full monthly set runs on a dependable cadence, and you're a regular presence where commodity analysts gather. By twelve months clients are giving direct, positive feedback on our insights, the content is generating inbound interest, and Treefera is being asked for comment on the commodities we cover — because the market knows you.
### **Who you’ll work with**
You’ll report to Jonathan and partner day-to-day with the Science & AI team, Product Marketing, and Sales & Marketing, while spending regular time with our clients and the commodity analysts who shape the market conversation.
### **Interview process & what to expect**
Recruiter screen (30–45 min)
Hiring manager interview (45–60 min)
Team & skills session (45–60 min)

**Tripledot** **Studios** is one of the largest independent mobile games companies in the world.

Our ambition is to be the most successful games company in the world, and we’re just getting started.
**The role is working within our studio: Tripledot Games**
**About Tripledot Games**
Tripledot Games is a leading developer and publisher of casual and puzzle games, with a strong presence in London, Warsaw, and Barcelona. The studio is responsible for multiple top 10 titles, including Woodoku, Woodoku Blast, Solitaire, and TripleTile. Our best-in-class data-driven approach spans the entire lifecycle from publishing to machine learning puzzle levels, helping us make fast, smart decisions at every stage of development.
We are also one of the largest IAA operators worldwide. Tripledot Games is a diverse and collaborative studio, home to people from over 36 nationalities. We take pride in our craftsmanship, strong focus on outcomes, and continuous improvement, building high-quality, scalable games that players around the world love.
## Role Overview
As a Data Scientist in our Experimentation team, you will help deliver and improve Tripledot’s company-wide experimentation analysis platform. Working closely with Data Engineering, you will define the statistical logic and methodologies behind platform features, build prototypes in Python, and ensure the platform produces accurate, reliable results for product teams across our games portfolio.
Your initial focus will include hands-on quality assurance: running independent analyses, comparing results with platform outputs, investigating discrepancies, and validating features and metrics. This offers the opportunity to develop deep expertise in experimentation and A/B testing across a sophisticated internal platform. As the platform evolves, the role will expand into more advanced statistical and machine learning work that delivers value across the business.
**Key Responsibilities**
* Define statistical logic, calculation methods, and detailed requirements for experimentation platform features.
* Prototype statistical methodologies and analyses in Python before implementation.
* Partner closely with Data Engineers as they develop and improve the experimentation platform.
* Perform thorough data and feature QA by independently calculating results and comparing them with platform outputs.
* Investigate discrepancies, identify root causes, and help ensure metrics and analyses are accurate and reliable.
* Explore opportunities to automate QA processes and improve the efficiency and quality of validation.
* Build a deep understanding of experimentation methodologies, including A/B testing, monitoring, segmentation, and analysis.
* Collaborate with BI, Machine Learning, product teams, and other stakeholders to understand requests and shape effective solutions.
* Contribute to future statistical, algorithmic, and machine learning initiatives as the team’s priorities evolve.
## Skills, Knowledge and Expertise
* 3-5 years of professional experience as a Data Scientist or in a closely related role
* Strong Python skills, including the ability to prototype analyses and write clear, reliable scripts.
* Solid knowledge of statistics and standard statistical methodologies.
* Practical understanding of experimentation and A/B testing, including how metrics and results should be calculated and validated.
* Familiarity with machine learning methods and the ability to apply relevant approaches when needed.
* Excellent attention to detail and a disciplined approach to repetitive or methodical QA work.
* Strong problem-solving skills, with the initiative to propose creative solutions and process improvements.
* Clear communication skills and the ability to explain analytical methods, results, and rationale.
* Experience with experimentation platforms or high-volume digital products, such as gaming, e-commerce, or ride-hailing, would be valuable.
* Ability to critically evaluate and validate AI-generated code, analyses, or modelling suggestions to ensure correctness and reproducibility.
* Experience using AI-assisted tools (e.g. code assistants or analytical copilots) to accelerate data exploration, research prototyping, and development workflows while maintaining scientific and statistical rigor.
* Interest in exploring AI-driven approaches that improve experimentation platforms, developer productivity, or data science research workflows.

We build AI agents for banks, taking on the manual work that stops them from growing.

We've raised $7 million from Northzone, Connect Ventures and TriplePoint, and work with acquiring banks including Worldpay, Barclaycard and NatWest.
We're earlier than that list makes us sound. The problem is real, and banks are already paying us to solve it. We're still experimenting with the product that best surfaces our value, and that's a large part of this job, rather than something that will be handed to you finished.
Doing that work is a small but driven team of 12 based in our Shoreditch office who care about their work and its impact.
There's also something you might already know us for. We built the UK's first payments price comparison platform, helping small businesses compare providers. It still runs today on MoneySuperMarket, Uswitch and money.co.uk. You won't be working on it, but it's why we know this market so well.
## How we work
* Extreme ownership: you own the outcome of your work, not just the output. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom and the responsibility to fix it.
* Learning velocity: curious, adaptable, and quick to pick things up. Hard problems require grit, and we embrace them.
* Customer-centric: we spend a day a week inside our partner banks, watching problems happen before they're even reported. Product decisions get made in that room, not in a roadmap meeting.
* Open and direct: we communicate openly, directly, and with intent.
## What you'll do
* Prototype, validate and ship full-stack features
* Design APIs and cloud architecture for agent workloads
* Keep the platform scalable, secure, and fast
* Spend time with our partner banks in their offices, and turn what you see there into product changes
## What we look for
We're hiring mid- to senior-level individual contributors with at least 4 years' experience.
* Depth in the modern web stack: React, Node.js, TypeScript, Python, AWS
* Strong product intuition: you think like a user
* Systems design you can explain and defend
* Experience deploying and running applications in the cloud
* Novel, interesting use of AI in your own work, and the ability to bring that to the team
We're an early-stage and intentionally lean. That means:
* We judge impact by the outcome of work, not the output
* Priorities shift when we learn something new, and we try to communicate why, but it happens
* You'll be given a direction, and the plan is yours to work out
This suits people who are comfortable with ambiguity, ask early when context is missing, and would rather ship something good enough fast than perfect something late.
It's less suited for those who prefer clear hierarchies, detailed briefs, or predictable roadmaps. That's not a character flaw; we just don't offer that yet.
Probation is a mutual check-in. We give feedback as we go, and we expect the same in return. If the fit isn't there, we'd rather know at month two than month six.

We're earlier than that list makes us sound. The problem is real, and banks are already paying us to solve it. We're still experimenting with the product that best surfaces our value, and that's a large part of this job, rather than something that will be handed to you finished.
Doing that work is a small but driven team of 12 based in our Shoreditch office who care about their work and its impact.
There's also something you might already know us for. We built the UK's first payments price comparison platform, helping small businesses compare providers. It still runs today on MoneySuperMarket, Uswitch and money.co.uk. You won't be working on it, but it's why we know this market so well.
## How we work
* Extreme ownership: you own the outcome of your work, not just the output. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom and the responsibility to fix it.
* Learning velocity: curious, adaptable, and quick to pick things up. Hard problems require grit, and we embrace them.
* Customer-centric: we spend a day a week inside our partner banks, watching problems happen before they're even reported. Product decisions get made in that room, not in a roadmap meeting.
* Open and direct: we communicate openly, directly, and with intent.
## What you'll do
* Develop and optimise AI agents for live banking workflows
* Design review gates, fail-safes, and fallback behaviour
* Build the observability and feedback loops behind agent performance
* Spend time with our partner banks in their offices, and turn what you see there into product changes
## What we look for
We're hiring mid- to senior-level individual contributors with at least 4 years' experience.
* Exceptional Python and experience orchestrating LLMs with tools like Temporal or LangChain
* AI automation shipped and running in production
* A record of making agents reliable and efficient
* Fluency with data pipelines and integrations
We're an early-stage and intentionally lean. That means:
* We judge impact by the outcome of work, not the output
* Priorities shift when we learn something new, and we try to communicate why, but it happens
* You'll be given a direction, and the plan is yours to work out
This suits people who are comfortable with ambiguity, ask early when context is missing, and would rather ship something good enough fast than perfect something late.
It's less suited for those who prefer clear hierarchies, detailed briefs, or predictable roadmaps. That's not a character flaw; we just don't offer that yet.
Probation is a mutual check-in. We give feedback as we go, and we expect the same in return. If the fit isn't there, we'd rather know at month two than month six.
## How you'll be assessed
Our aim is to get candidates through the whole process within two weeks of applying — quick enough to respect your time, thorough enough to keep our standards high.

04

05
30-minute conversation with our CEO, Ed, to close things out and answer anything still on your mind
## What's in it for you
* A competitive salary and generous equity
* Three days a week in our Shoreditch office, Tuesday to Thursday, and the rest wherever you work best
* 25 days holiday, with flexibility when you need it
* £350 a year towards taking a proper break

## Description
The operations we automate run on work that has never been fully written down. There is usually a process document, and it usually describes the standard case. The parts that matter most sit with the people doing the work every day. That is why this work has resisted automation for so long, and why AI agents that can exercise judgement change what is possible.
As an AI Deployment Lead you own the deployment of our Virtual Agents end to end. You lead the customer through delivery, work out how their operation actually runs, agree what we are building and what we are not, and work alongside our Implementation Engineers to get it live and converted.
You are not a project coordinator. You are the person the customer trusts to understand their operation, and the person our engineers rely on to know what to build.
You'll join as our first AI Deployment Lead, working closely with product and engineering to build and mature the function, with an opportunity to step into a leadership role in future.
## Requirements
**About the role:**
* **Own deployments end to end.** Lead the engagement from kickoff through to a live, adopted automation. Set the plan, align stakeholders across operations, IT and the executive team, and hold everyone including the customer accountable to it
* **Discover how the work is really done.** Work alongside customer teams to understand the process as it exists rather than as it is documented: the volumes, the exceptions, the judgement calls, the decisions nobody wrote down. Turn that into a clear, agreed scope our engineers can build against and our customers recognise as their own. We're looking for people who are able to document the SOP, not only run the workshop
* **Advise on what to automate and what to leave.** Not every part of a process should be automated on day one. You make the trade-offs explicit, sequence what lands first, and make sure the customer understands what they're getting
* **Deliver alongside engineering.** Our Implementation Engineers own the technical design and build. You own the agreed customer outcome, scope and requirements, and you're close enough to the product to challenge a design, discuss access and integrations, and understand what's feasible
* **Define success and drive the decision.** Agree what good looks like and how it will be measured, capture the customer's baseline before we build, and lead the conversation that turns a pilot into a production service
* **Make the next deployment faster.** Turn what you learn into playbooks, patterns and product requirements. You're often the earliest signal on what our product needs to do next
**About you:**
* 5+ years in management, technology or transformation consulting, implementation or professional services, including time at AI Deployment Lead, Engagement Manager, Project Leader or equivalent level where you owned a programme end to end. We're looking for people who have run the engagement, not only staffed it
* Experience working inside complex operations and turning them into structure that technical teams can act on. Comfortable with processes that are messy, undocumented and internally contested

* Technically fluent. You don't need to code, but you need to hold your own with engineers on integrations, access, data and feasibility
* Strong stakeholder presence. Comfortable with an operations team on Monday and an executive steering group on Tuesday, and able to build credibility quickly
* Comfortable handling objections and navigating organisational resistance. Automation changes how people work, and not everyone in the room wants it to succeed
* Highly analytical, ruthlessly organised and detail-oriented
* Highly autonomous and entrepreneurial, and comfortable in an environment where the playbook is still being written

* Experience working with customers in insurance, healthcare or another regulated operational environment
* Prior experience at a startup or high-growth company where you built process from scratch

# Masters Degree in Data Center Leadership and Management
### Data centers need highly capable leaders and managers - individuals who are capable of dealing with business complexity and technological change with the knowledge and skills to ensure their teams deliver against consistently challenging objectives.
## Program Overview
Join the global elite group of data center professionals from IBM, Commscope, Schneider Electric, Time Warner Cable, Sudlows Limited, Unilever, Capital One, University of Melbourne, Microsoft to name a few.
Data centers are complex facilities that are expected to deliver faultless service and financial results in a world of rapidly changing technologies, business pressures and environmental expectations.
In order to achieve this, data centers need highly capable leaders and managers - individuals who are capable of dealing with business complexity and technological change with the knowledge and skills to ensure their teams deliver against consistently challenging objectives.
The Masters Degree in Data Center Leadership and Management is a unique program, which has been designed in collaboration with the industry to advance data center professionals worldwide. No other university program offers data center professionals this high level leadership and management education tailored to the data center sector.
The program harnesses CNet's unique insight into data center operations and expertise in business leadership and management. Topics have been selected on the basis of feedback from the industry and data center professionals who are themselves involved with delivering the program alongside other hand-picked specialists. The content of the Masters Degree is reviewed and refreshed each year to ensure it reflects the constantly evolving nature of the sector.
Delivery of the program is through distance learning, meaning that learners can study at times that are convenient to them. They can also easily communicate with their tutors and each other wherever they are in the world.
### **Structure**
Primarily this three year program is based around supported online distance learning via a learning management system, providing flexibility and complete interaction every step of the way. Learners will be supported by the CNet team, specialist academic staff and industry specialists, all with the aim of creating an enriched shared learning experience. There is an optional bootcamp held every two years in Cambridge, UK for those who wish to attend.
On average, learners commit the equivalent of approximately 10 hours of study per week to the program during trimester time, which can be taken at your own pace and at a convenient time for you. However, the deadlines that are given for your assessed work are strict and must be met.
The program is run across two learning periods per year consisting of 12 weeks of teaching. This will include online learning content, regular virtual tutorials (usually an hour in duration at dates and times published at the start of the program), and online discussion forums with peers and the academic tutor. There is one point of entry per year in September. Each module is formally assessed.
### **Masters Degree Application Process**
If you have any questions or are interested in applying for the program, please fill out the Request Follow-Up form on this page to contact our Education team.
#### Request Follow-Up
*You can unsubscribe at any time by contacting us or following the unsubscribe instructions in our emails.*
*Your information will be processed in accordance with our*
* Evolution of leadership
* Complexity theory, dynamic organizational environments, strategic alignment in organizations, systems theory
* Emergent leadership theory in dynamic environments
* Internal business environment analysis and organizational dynamics
* Models of strategic analysis
* The role of leaders in fostering cultures of innovation, creativity and change capability in dynamic environments
* Change management
* Asset tracking ("Cradle to Grave")
* Change management
* Analysis of virtual/logical systems and how they interact with physical hardware
* Management & resilience high capacity storage in complex data centers (especially related to disaster recovery scenarios)
* Consolidation of resources/locations
* Optimising physical infrastructure (including space management) to enable higher capacity
* Multi-layered monitoring
* Future strategic planning via modelling scenarios
* Physical security & data security
* Virtual digital security (especially in co-location environments)
* Identification of data center infrastructure risks and vulnerabilities, mitigation techniques and recovery policies
* Governance relating to data protection, safe harbour and other compliance regimes.
* Evaluation metrics
* Managing human resources for optimal performance
* Organisational behaviour
* Developing and managing structures for continued capability growth
* Managing contractor arrangements and a contingent workforce
* Knowledge management
The final year expands your horizons even further, giving you the chance to develop your thought leadership and address specific business issues. First, in the "Contemporary Issues in Leadership and Management" module, you will explore themes in the data center sector and gain an in depth understanding of issues that are important to you. Next, you will develop your research skills, giving you the expertise to frame, plan and deliver research - this will provide a platform for your academic studies and will also enable you to develop new, credible and robust knowledge in your business. Finally, you will put all of your learning into practice by developing and delivering a major project ("dissertation" or "thesis"). You can look at this as a piece of work which could address a live issue in your workplace, or be based on a theme in the data center sector as a whole. Your major project will be one of the defining moments of your Masters Degree program and could open the door to further study or career development.
****Contemporary Issues in Leadership and Management****
* Leadership and CSR
* Technology advancements and implications
* Sustainability and environmental issues
* Globalisation and offshoring
* Standards and quality management
* Other topics as identified by industry partners
****Research Methods & Post Graduate Major Project****
* Intellectual and practical skills to frame, plan and deliver research
* Analysis and interpretation of data generated
* Bringing this into action through a major research project, based on your own interests and providing a culmination of your work on the Masters program.
This program has been designed for people in leadership and management positions within data center facilities. CNet Training will consider all applications individually, taking into account each applicant's experience and qualifications. We encourage you to apply if you:
* Work in a data center facility
* Have at least two years at middle or senior management level in a data center context
It would be advantageous if you have a first or second class degree from a UK university, or equivalent from an overseas university.
Those applicants for whom English is not a first language will be expected to demonstrate a certificated level of proficiency of at least IELTS 6.5 or equivalent.
Program Requirements
The aim of this Degree is to unite the existing knowledge and skills of data center professionals with essential new learning centered around leadership and management within a data center environment and award a top level degree qualification.
You will also gain the following:
* Masters Degree in Data Center Leadership & Management (MA) - a Level 7 qualification.
* Use of MA post nominal letters after your name e.g. *Martin Smith MA*
* Use of the official Masters Degree in Data Center Leadership (MA) Digital Badge

You'll join our web team, working alongside front-end engineers and our Software Engineer in Test, and reporting to the Lead Frontend Engineer. It's a team where curiosity meets craft: we blend creativity, technical excellence and a strong product mindset to create experiences that feel simple, rewarding and built to last.
## Why This Role Matters
**Why the role exists**
We're looking for a hands-on Frontend Software Engineer who can own front-end craft and extend it end to end - from the interfaces our customers use to the Cloudflare Workers and light backend services that power them.
This is an individual contributor role with plenty of influence. You'll build with React and TypeScript, work on API routes, integrations and edge logic using Cloudflare Workers, and help make AI-first, verify-second engineering the team's default.
You'll partner with the Lead Frontend Engineer on architecture, with Product and Design on user experience, and with our Software Engineer in Test on quality. You'll set direction through the quality of your code, reviews and judgement, rather than through formal authority.
We're looking for someone who asks why, not just what. You'll be curious about our customers and commercial goals, challenge assumptions constructively and help us spot valuable opportunities before they arrive as tickets. This is a UK-based hybrid role, including time with the team in Leeds, and may include occasional travel to our European and other international locations as we grow.
### **What success looks like**
* Ship polished, accessible and high-performing customer experiences built on strong React and TypeScript foundations.
* Deliver features end to end, including the Cloudflare Workers, APIs and integrations behind the interface.
* Use AI tooling as a genuine development partner while checking, testing and improving every output before it ships.
* Build quality in from the start through testable code, unit and component coverage, and close partnership with our Software Engineer in Test.
* Raise the technical bar for front-end craft, edge architecture and full-stack judgement across the web team.
* Turn customer and business insight into better product decisions, not just completed tickets.
# **What You’ll Do**
**Customer experience and front-end craft**
* Build and maintain customer-facing experiences. We currently use Astro and React, but prioritise selecting the right tool for each challenge over adherence to any single framework.
* Turn design intent into polished, resilient interfaces, partnering closely with Product and Design.
* Own responsive layouts, cross-browser compatibility and progressive enhancement across our brand portfolio.
* Build accessibility (WCAG), Core Web Vitals, component quality and sensible front-end caching into everyday engineering decisions.
**Full-stack and edge delivery**
* Deliver features end to end across our Cloudflare Workers stack—API routes, edge logic, integrations—using Wrangler, D1, KV and R2.
* Build and maintain integrations with forms, CRM and marketing tools such as HubSpot, and headless CMS platforms such as Storyblok.
* Make sound architectural decisions on the edge platform, leveraging Cloudflare's caching, KV and CDN to keep our infrastructure lean.
* Consider internationalisation and localisation as our products and edge logic adapt for different markets.
**AI-first, quality-first engineering**
* Use agentic AI tooling, including Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor or similar, for scaffolding, refactoring, debugging and documentation.
* Treat AI output as a starting point: run type-checks and tests, verify API and library claims against official documentation, and keep human judgement around any meaningful risk.
* Write your own unit and component tests with Vitest, React Testing Library or similar, and partner with our Software Engineer in Test on end-to-end, visual regression and accessibility automation.
* Integrate work cleanly through Git, GitHub Actions and our Jira-based Agile workflow, contributing thoughtfully to planning, stand-ups and retrospectives.
**Technical leadership and continuous improvement**
* Shape front-end and edge architecture through high-quality code, constructive reviews and mentoring by example, working with the Lead Frontend Engineer on strategic decisions.
* Improve the codebase and team workflows, staying current with the front-end and AI landscape and bringing back credible, proven ideas.
* Write clear, structured code and documentation that both people and AI agents can understand and work with.
## What You’ll Bring
## **Essential**
* Substantial hands-on experience as a front-end-focused full-stack engineer, with a track record of senior-level ownership. This is often built over five or more years, but depth and judgement matter more than an exact number.
* Strong, idiomatic React and confidence across the modern JavaScript and TypeScript ecosystem.
* A strong grasp of front-end craft, including UI and UX sensibility, responsive design, cross-browser compatibility, progressive enhancement and maintainable component architecture.
* Confidence extending into backend development through Cloudflare Workers or an equivalent edge or serverless platform, plus Node-based API services.
* Practical, regular use of AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot or Cursor, with good judgement about when to trust, verify or reject their output.
* Experience with a headless CMS such as Storyblok and third-party integrations, including forms and CRM or marketing platforms such as HubSpot.
* A working understanding of accessibility, Core Web Vitals and caching across the browser, CDN and edge as everyday engineering concerns.
* A habit of writing your own unit and component tests using Vitest, React Testing Library or similar, alongside effective collaboration with a dedicated quality function.
* Confidence with Git, Agile delivery and CI/CD pipelines such as GitHub Actions.
* Sound architectural judgement, clear communication and the confidence to shape technical direction without formal authority.
* A proactive mindset: you investigate, ask why and propose better options rather than waiting for a ticket to define every next step.
## **Helpful**
* Experience with internationalisation or localisation in front-end or edge applications.
* Exposure to agentic AI workflows or MCP-based tooling, such as Playwright MCP or Storyblok MCP.
* Experience partnering with a QA or SDET function on end-to-end, visual regression or accessibility automation.
* Familiarity with performance testing tools such as Lighthouse or similar..
* A background in e-commerce or re-commerce platforms.

No specific qualifications are required. We care about the work you've done, the judgement you bring and how you keep learning.
