job_description:
# Apply for Engineering Manager, Runtime Platform, Robot Software London, United Kingdom Vehicle SW Engineering
## **About us**
Founded in 2017, Wayve is the leading developer of Embodied AI technology. Our advanced AI software and foundation models enable vehicles to perceive, understand, and navigate any complex environment, enhancing the usability and safety of automated driving systems.
Our vision is to create autonomy that propels the world forward. Our intelligent, mapless, and hardware-agnostic AI products are designed for automakers, accelerating the transition from assisted to automated driving.
In our fast-paced environment big problems ignite us—we embrace uncertainty, leaning into complex challenges to unlock groundbreaking solutions. We aim high and stay humble in our pursuit of excellence, constantly learning and evolving as we pave the way for a smarter, safer future.
At Wayve, your contributions matter. We value diversity, embrace new perspectives, and foster an inclusive work environment; we back each other to deliver impact.
Make Wayve the experience that defines your career!
## About The Team
Wayve is building embodied AI that can drive any vehicle, anywhere. Our AI Driver runs on-vehicle in real time, and the **Runtime Platform team** owns the application frameworks, middleware (IPC / inter-process communication), monitoring, performance, and observability foundations that make that possible. This is a growing sub-team that we're breaking out into its own team, and you’ll be the Engineering Manager to lead it.
## The role
As Engineering Manager for Runtime Platform, you'll lead a single team and be accountable for its delivery, engagement, resourcing, roadmap, and performance. People leadership is your first priority: you'll coach and grow the team, keep it engaged and high-performing, and own hiring as the team stands up. You'll pair that with strong technical judgment — setting clear technical direction on latency, profiling, real-time scheduling, and middleware, and owning the outcome of the team's technical decisions.
## What you'll do
* **Lead and grow the team (first priority):** keep the team engaged, developing, and performing with good morale; run 1:1s, set clear expectations, give regular high-quality feedback, manage performance, and support career growth against our career framework.
* **Hire and build the team:** own hiring and onboarding to get the right people in the right roles, and shape the team's culture and ways of working as it forms.
* **Drive execution:** ensure the team's work advances company goals; staff committed programs, keep the roadmap aligned to available resources, prioritize, and hold the team accountable for delivery, quality, and operational reliability.
* **Set technical direction:** ensure the team has a clear, holistic technical direction and clear ownership of its technology-roadmap milestones — working closely with the team's tech lead(s) and stakeholders; own the outcome of the team's technical decisions.
* **Own the runtime foundations:** guide the team's work across system design, application frameworks, the middleware/IPC layer, performance & optimization, and measurement & observability. Enable new vehicle platform enablement with incremental work and minimal performance degradation. Implement and maintain strong CI, HIL, and internal quality gates to provide a robust framework for fast iteration..
* **Collaborate and unblock:** cascade the roadmap, partner with internal Vehicle Software teams, model developers, hardware, and OEM programs. Act as the point of escalation for your team, and proactively surface and resolve risks and dependencies.
## What you'll bring
* **Engineering management experience (essential):** a track record of leading, growing, engaging, and retaining a high-performing software/systems team — including hiring, coaching, feedback, and performance management. People management is your first priority.
* **Delivery through a team:** experience owning a team's roadmap and shipping through others — planning, prioritization, resourcing, and accountability for quality and operational reliability.
* **Technical credibility:** hands-on depth in what takes to architect and deliver embedded software shipped on a product to real customers. Demonstrate knowledge of high-performance, low-latency embedded software (C++) to earn the trust of senior systems engineers and own the team's technical decisions. You don't need to be the team's top individual contributor.
* **Performance & systems fundamentals:** solid understanding of profiling, benchmarking, latency/throughput/memory-bandwidth analysis, and real-time scheduling, on embedded Linux (ideally also QNX).
* **IPC / middleware:** a strong grasp of middleware for high-throughput real-time or robotics systems and the trade-offs across vendors and platforms.
* **Cross-functional leadership:** the ability to set direction and deliver through influence across many stakeholder teams.
## Nice to have
* Experience in automotive, robotics, or another safety-relevant real-time domain.
* Familiarity with profiling toolchains (pprof/gperftools, perf, Nsight, NVLumo) and observability stacks (OpenTelemetry, Grafana, Datadog).
* Experience with NVIDIA (Orin/Thor) and/or Qualcomm compute platforms.
* Experience with a micro-kernel and/or real-time OS (e.g. QNX) is a plus.
## Why this team
The Runtime Platform team supports Wayve's on-vehicle stack — other on-board components rely on the frameworks, performance, observability, and layers it owns. You'll lead a team whose work contributes to how Wayve scales its AI Driver to new vehicles, OEM programs, and other embodiments.
This is a full-time role based in our office in London. At Wayve we want the best of all worlds so we operate a hybrid working policy that combines time together in our offices and workshops to fuel innovation, culture, relationships and learning, and time spent working from home. We operate core working hours so you can determine the schedule that works best for you and your team.

Since the project, we’ve provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

Wifinity was founded in 2007 to solve a problem - our armed forces were struggling with reliable connectivity. While living in barracks, often in remote locations, ordering a landline and booking in an engineer just wasn't an option.

We take the complexity out of connectivity.
**The Opportunity:**We are looking for a Senior FP&A Manager to own financial planning and analysis for the Group. This is a high-impact, hands-on role with visibility to the executive team, board, investor and lenders. You will own the annual budget, reforecast and rolling forecast cycles, long-range planning, the models behind major capital and commercial decisions, and the analysis and commentary that help senior stakeholders understand performance and choose between options.
The role reports to the Commercial Finance Director, has one direct report, a Commercial Finance Analyst, and sits alongside financial control and business partnering. You will build and own models yourself, while improving planning discipline across finance and the business and helping close the gap between senior stakeholder expectations and current systems, data and process maturity.
**Key Responsibilities:**The role is built around five priorities...
**Planning & Forecasting**
* Own the **annual budget process** end-to-end, including the timetable, templates, assumptions, budget holder challenge and consolidation, building plans from operational drivers rather than extrapolation.
* Own the **reforecast and rolling forecast** cycles for P&L, cash flow, working capital and capex, including project phasing, pipeline assumptions, cash low points and risks and opportunities.
* Own the **operational long-range model**, including scenario, sensitivity and downside cases used to test funding requirements, keeping it robust, documented and usable by others.
* Drive **forecast accuracy** as a discipline, tracking variances back to their causes and tightening the assumptions, and the underlying data, that repeatedly prove unreliable.
**Analysis, Insight & Decision Support**
* Produce **analysis that explains performance**, not just reports it, linking variance, margin, mix and operational drivers to a clear view of what changed, why it matters and action required.
* Own the **group KPI framework and the unit economics** beneath it, keeping the set tiered, mutually exclusive and genuinely decision-useful.
* Support **post-acquisition activity**, including the financial integration of acquired businesses into group planning and reporting, where definitions, data structures and reporting conventions will differ from our own.
* Provide **ad hoc analysis** for commercial, operational and corporate decisions, often at short notice and from partial information, setting out assumptions, confidence level and what would need to be true to change the answer.
**Reporting & Communication**
* Own the **forward-looking elements of monthly reporting** and the planning and performance content within board and investor packs, ensuring output is accurate, consistent and presented to an infrastructure investor standard.
* Write **clear, honest commentary** that gives senior stakeholders a defensible view of where performance is heading, the basis of the numbers and the limitations in the data, using simple financial storytelling for non-finance audiences.
* Support any **lending requirements**, including covenant forecasting and testing, headroom analysis, liquidity monitoring and drawdown scenarios.
* Respond to **investor and board questions** with speed and confidence, including unplanned scenario questions, and present forecasts, scenarios and performance messages clearly.
**Systems, Data & Process**
* Act as the **FP&A voice in the planned finance systems migration** from Access to a new ERP, defining planning, reporting and data requirements and testing that they are met.
* Redevelop and maintain the planning environment, including a rebuild in Adaptive, so that **forecasting is faster**, better controlled and less dependent on manual manipulation.
* Work with finance and operational data owners to **improve data integrity**, definitions and lineage, identifying where information does not reconcile and proposing resolution.
* **Automate recurring reporting and build dashboards**, applying analytics and AI tooling pragmatically where it improves quality, speed or insight.
* **Reduce key person risk** by documenting models, standardising templates and making the planning process repeatable.
**Leadership & Partnering**
* **Manage, coach and develop** a Commercial Finance Analyst, setting analytical standards and creating the space for that person to grow.
* Act as a **trusted partner** to the executive team and to leaders across sales, marketing, delivery, network operations and transformation.
* **Coordinate and challenge inputs** from finance business partners, commercial pricing and project control so that group plans are consistent and credible.
* **Raise financial literacy** across the business, helping budget holders understand the drivers behind their numbers, drive their forecasts and translate finance into operational actions.
**About you:**You are a commercially minded finance professional who is energised by building, improving and influencing, not just reporting. You are technically strong on modelling and forecasting, and comfortable translating commercial ambition into financial arithmetic. You can separate what matters from what is merely measurable, challenge assumptions with evidence, and form a defensible view from incomplete or conflicting information. You are organised, resilient under pressure and willing to roll your sleeves up in a business still building its planning infrastructure.
Essential experience:
* Significant FP&A experience, including demonstrable ownership of a full budget cycle and the reforecast process at group or business unit level.
* Strong three-statement modelling capability, with proven experience building and maintaining driver-based models, long-range plans and scenario and sensitivity analysis.
* Grounding in the technical building blocks of the role: unit economics, contract profitability and revenue recognition in long-term service contracts, cash flow and working capital forecasting, and investment appraisal using IRR, NPV and payback.
* Track record of producing material and commentary for board, investor and lender audiences, with the confidence to explain and defend the analysis.
* Examples of building planning or reporting from inconsistent data sources, and improving those inputs over time rather than continuing to work around them.
* Experience partnering with senior non-finance stakeholders, including at executive level, and presenting financial messages in a way that is clear, tailored and action-oriented.
* Evidence of improving planning and reporting processes, not simply operating those inherited.
* Line management or coaching experience, or a clear readiness to take on a first direct report.
Desirable but not essential:
* Experience in a private equity or infrastructure-backed business, including investor reporting, covenant reporting or lender engagement, or in an SME or scaling business where reporting disciplines are still being built.

# **Support Engineer**

## **Wordsmith**
Wordsmith is building the legal operating system for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.
We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems.
Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgement matters, and every step is captured as work happens.
We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend and become a function the business can run with.
More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by over $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.
## **The role**
We’re hiring a Support Engineer to provide fast, thoughtful and technically rigorous help to Wordsmith customers.
You’ll own technical questions and incidents from first response through to resolution. You’ll understand what the customer is trying to achieve, reproduce reported behaviour, investigate the underlying cause and explain the outcome clearly.
This is more than scripted customer support. You’ll be expected to investigate application behaviour at a technical level, including reading logs and tracing issues through the product and its codebase. Where appropriate to your experience, you may also propose and submit code fixes through our normal engineering review and release process.
Wordsmith supports customers globally through a follow-the-sun model. You’ll work the standard hours for your region and hand over unresolved issues clearly to colleagues in other regions. There is no routine expectation that you work another region’s hours.
## **What you’ll do**
* Own technical support requests — triage, investigate and resolve customer questions and incidents from first response to confirmed resolution.
* Diagnose problems thoroughly — gather the right context, reproduce reported behaviour, inspect logs and data, and trace issues through the product and codebase.
* Resolve technical issues — correct configuration or usage problems directly and collaborate with Engineering when a product or infrastructure change is required.
* Contribute code fixes where appropriate — depending on your experience, propose and submit well-tested fixes through the standard engineering review and deployment process.
* Communicate clearly — give customers timely and accurate updates, explain technical issues without unnecessary jargon and set honest expectations.
* Manage escalations — bring in Engineering, Product or other specialists when needed while retaining ownership of the case and its communication.
* Support global handovers — document investigation, impact, current status and next actions so colleagues in another region can continue work without losing momentum.
* Protect service quality — recognise high-impact incidents quickly, follow the appropriate escalation process and contribute to incident reviews.
* Build customer knowledge — create and maintain troubleshooting guides, known-issue documentation and help-centre content.
* Reduce repeat problems — identify patterns in support demand and recommend improvements to the product, documentation, tooling and customer experience.
* Improve support operations — help develop service levels, escalation paths, reporting and technical-support processes as the function scales.
## **What we’re looking for**
* Experience in technical support, product support, software engineering, solutions engineering or another customer-facing technical role.
* Strong diagnostic ability — you can work methodically from symptoms to root cause rather than relying on guesswork.
* A working understanding of modern web applications, APIs, authentication, integrations and common browser or network issues.
* Experience using diagnostic information such as application logs, monitoring tools, browser developer tools and database queries.
* Enough familiarity with software code to navigate a codebase, follow application logic and use it to investigate reported behaviour.
* Clear customer communication — you can remain calm under pressure, set expectations honestly and explain complex issues at the right level of detail.
* Strong ownership — you remain responsible for moving an issue forward even when other teams need to contribute.
* Sound prioritisation — you can assess urgency and customer impact and recognise when an issue requires immediate escalation.
* Care and precision — you document what you tested, avoid unsupported conclusions and confirm that the customer’s problem has actually been resolved.
* Interest in AI systems — you’re curious about how AI-enabled products behave and comfortable investigating issues that may not always be deterministic.
* No legal background is required, but you should be motivated to learn how in-house legal teams work.
### **Desirable, but not essential**
* Experience writing and debugging production software.
* The ability to create automated tests and submit code fixes for engineering review.
* Experience supporting AI-enabled or data-intensive applications.
* Familiarity with incident-management and observability tools.
## **How we work**
We’re an in-person team based in Edinburgh. You should expect to work from the office as your default.
We support customers globally using a follow-the-sun model. You’ll work the normal hours agreed for your region and create clear handovers when an issue needs to continue beyond them. Any exceptional on-call or out-of-hours arrangements would be agreed and communicated separately.
We set a high bar, move quickly and give people meaningful ownership. Support is a core part of the product experience, and we expect it to be technically credible, responsive and human.
You’ll work closely with Engineering, Product, Transformation and Customer Success. Customer Success owns adoption and customer health; Transformation owns implementation; Account Management owns renewals and commercial growth; and Support Engineering owns technical investigation and resolution.
## **Why Wordsmith**
You’ll support a fast-growing product used for important work inside some of the world’s most ambitious organisations.
Because we’re building in a new technical category, the problems are interesting. You’ll work across software behaviour, integrations, data and AI systems rather than following a script.
You’ll have the opportunity to shape our support tooling and operating model, influence the product through direct customer evidence, and develop towards senior support engineering, support leadership, solutions engineering or product engineering.

Job Description:
Are you passionate about creating memorable player experiences that delight millions of players every day? Do you thrive on solving complex design challenges that span multiple systems, teams and player journeys?
We're looking for a strategic and creative Senior Game Designer to join the Player Value team in Candy Crush Saga. In this role, you'll shape some of the most important moments in a player's experience, from their first session through their long-term journey, creating experiences that maximize player value, engagement and delight. You'll have the opportunity to influence the game at a holistic level, working across multiple initiatives and collaborating with teams throughout Candy Crush Saga.
Your role within the Kingdom
As a Senior Game Designer in the Player Value team, you'll work in a collaborative, fast-paced environment alongside Product Managers, UX Designers, Data Scientists, Engineers and other Game Designers to identify and redesign the moments that matter most to players.
You'll think beyond individual features, taking a holistic view of the player journey to create cohesive experiences that improve onboarding, progression, motivation, retention and long-term engagement. From reimagining the first-time user experience to evolving key player journeys, you'll connect insights across the game and drive design strategies that elevate the overall player experience.
Key Responsibilities
Own the design of high-impact player experiences that span multiple features, systems and teams.
Shape and evolve key player journeys, including onboarding, progression, rewards and other critical moments that influence long-term engagement.
Develop a holistic vision for player value, ensuring experiences feel meaningful, rewarding and cohesive throughout the game.
Drive discovery and concept development for strategic opportunities that improve player satisfaction, engagement and business outcomes.
Collaborate across multiple product teams to align experiences into a seamless player journey.
Create clear design documentation, player journey maps and experience frameworks to communicate vision and drive execution.
Use qualitative research, player feedback and quantitative data to identify friction points, uncover opportunities and validate design decisions.
Stay informed on market trends, player expectations and emerging design practices, bringing fresh thinking into the team.
Champion systems thinking, ensuring new experiences complement the broader Candy Crush ecosystem and reinforce long-term player value.
Skills
Strategic Thinker – Able to zoom out and design experiences from a player journey perspective, balancing immediate needs with long-term engagement.
Systems Designer – Comfortable designing across interconnected features and understanding how multiple systems combine to shape player experience.
Player-Centric – Passionate about understanding player motivations and creating experiences that surprise, delight and build lasting relationships with the game.
Analytical – Uses data, experimentation and player insights to inform decisions and continuously improve experiences.
Collaborative Influencer – Excels at working across disciplines and multiple teams, building alignment and driving initiatives that span organizational boundaries.
Creative Problem Solver – Brings innovative thinking to complex design challenges, identifying opportunities to create meaningful player value at scale.
Market Awareness – Deep understanding of casual and free-to-play games, player psychology and evolving industry trends.
Bonus Points
Experience designing player journeys, onboarding, progression, reward systems or engagement loops.
Experience driving initiatives that span multiple product teams or game systems.
Experience with UX, service design or product strategy.
Experience leading discovery work and defining product vision for ambiguous problem spaces.
About King
With a mission of Making the World Playful, King is a leading interactive entertainment company for the mobile world with more than 20 years of history of delivering some of the world’s most iconic games in the mobile gaming industry, including the world-famous Candy Crush franchise, as well as other mobile titles such as Farm Heroes Saga. King games are played by more than 200 million monthly active users. King, part of Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), has Kingsters in Stockholm, Malmö, London, Barcelona, Berlin, Dublin, San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles and Malta. ## Security Engineer
**London, England, United Kingdom**
Apply Online
**The Firm**
XTX Markets is a leading algorithmic trading firm which uses state-of-the-art machine learning technology to produce price forecasts for over 53,000 financial instruments across equities, fixed income, currencies, commodities and crypto. It uses those forecasts to trade on exchanges and alternative trading venues, and to offer differentiated liquidity directly to clients worldwide. The firm trades over $250bn a day across 35 countries and has over 300 employees based in London, Singapore, New York, Paris, Bristol, Mumbai, Yerevan and Kajaani.
We leverage the talent of the people who work here, modern computational techniques and state-of-the-art research infrastructure to analyse large data sets across markets quickly and efficiently, to maximize the effectiveness of our proprietary trading algorithms. We are actively seeking new methods and ideas. The models that drive our trading strategies have evolved considerably over the last 10 years, from econometric methods that gave our company its name, to trees, to neural networks, to modern deep learning architectures.
XTX Markets has an unrivalled level of computational resources in the trading industry, with a growing research cluster currently containing well over 25,000 GPUs with more than 1 exabyte of usable storage. Teams across the firm include world-class researchers, developers and technologists with backgrounds in pure math, programming, physics, computer science and machine learning. The firm is also constructing a large-scale data centre in Finland to future-proof its significant computational capabilities.
At XTX Markets technology is our business and we are a diverse organization which attracts outstanding talent from across all industry backgrounds. We are focused on teamwork and our people collaborate on all aspects of the business, working openly and with respect for each other, our clients and the market. Our culture is non-hierarchical and one where everyone is valued. We strive for excellence in everything we do.
**The Role**
The Information Security team at XTX Markets is accountable for all aspects of the firm’s IT security. From obtaining and transforming events and signals into actionable intelligence, to helping design and implement authentication and authorisation systems, and other security tools that underpin the XTX environment.
The team also assess third party security, as well as working diligently to keep XTX in compliance with a range of world-wide regulatory information security requirements.
Our Security team works to create and maintain the safest operating environment for XTX Markets users and developers. In this role, you will work with software engineers to proactively identify security flaws and engineer technical solutions to a defensive mindset.
This is a hands-on role. XTX prides itself on its ability to create and maintain software and systems that precisely meet our needs.
We handle information at large scale and across multiple locations, so we need to anticipate and protect against attackers. You will work closely with teams to improve our detection capabilities, and to design defence-in-depth controls that limit attackers' ability to move inside our network.
**Responsibilities** At XTX, security engineers are engaged in requirements gathering, architecting, prototyping, and developing both internal tools and broader infrastructure in conjunction with partner teams around XTX.
The successful candidate will be expected to work across a broad range of security roles and projects, including compliance related tasks.
**Essential Attributes**
* Approximately one to three years’ experience in Information Security.
* Proficiency in at least one statically typed language; development at XTX is primarily in Golang, though previous experience in Go is not a pre-requisite. Scripting is mainly in Python.
* Knowledge of how systems are built as well as how to break them.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
* Able to write clearly and succinctly.
* Rapid learner with strong attention to detail.
* Able to work autonomously and prioritise as required.
* Willing to admit mistakes and seek feedback to improve performance.
**Desirable Attributes**
* Personal projects which you can show or talk about.
* Experience playing CTFs.
* Security certifications demonstrating practical ability, e.g. OSCP.
**Benefits**
* Onsite gym, sauna, and fitness classes at no charge (Wellbeing Space).
* Extensive medical benefits including an on-site doctor and therapist at no charge.
* Breakfast and lunch provided daily.
* Various supports for caregivers, including emergency dependent care.
* Beautiful King’s Cross office: (Office Tour).
* 25 days paid holiday per year + statutory holiday and paid sick days.
* Generous Pension contributions.
* We work 4 days per week in the office, 1 from home unless stated otherwise.

**About zaimler**
AI agents can't reason over data they don't understand. Enterprise data today is fragmented across dozens of systems with no shared context, meaning, or structure, and that's why most enterprise AI is failing. The shift from copilots to autonomous agents is creating an entirely new infrastructure layer, and we're building it.
zaimler is the context infrastructure for the agentic era: a platform that automatically discovers domain knowledge, maps relationships, and gives AI agents the semantic understanding to operate with precision at scale. Imagine knowledge graphs that support real-time inference, built for systems that need to reason, not just retrieve.
zaimler was founded by Biswajit Das (ex-VP Engineering, Truera), a Data Infra veteran and former Chief Architect at Visa, and Sofus Macskassy (ex-Director of Engineering, LinkedIn), who built one of the largest knowledge graphs in production in the industry at LinkedIn. We're growing and deploying with major enterprises across insurance, travel, and technology. If you want to build infrastructure that the next decade of enterprise AI runs on, we'd love to talk.
**About the Job**
We're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to own the technical front line of our enterprise deals in EMEA.
This is not a quota-carrying sales role, and it is not a pure delivery role. You are the person who walks into a room with a customer's data architects, understands their environment faster than they expect you to, and shows them what becomes possible when their agents can actually reason over their data. Then you make it real. You run the proof of value, you convert it into a production proof of concept, and you carry everything you learned back to our engineering team so the product gets better.
You'll be one of the first people a customer meets and one of the last to leave before they're in production. That means the demo, the technical objection, the competitive comparison against our competitors, the architecture whiteboard with a skeptical principal engineer, and the honest read on whether a deal is real. All of it is yours.
We're a small team, so you'll help build the playbook rather than inherit one. This role requires regular travel to customer sites across the UK and Europe.
### What You Will Be Doing
* Run technical demos and discovery sessions with enterprise buyers, from data platform leads up to CIOs
* Build and own our pre-sales playbook: demo narratives, discovery frameworks, objection handling, and reference architectures
* Own the competitive landscape. Know where we win against Palantir, the hyperscalers, and the semantic layer vendors, and know honestly where we don't
* Drive proofs of value from scoping through to signed proof of concept, holding the technical thread the whole way
* Translate customer environments and edge cases into structured product feedback that reaches engineering with enough context to act on
* Partner with our ML and infrastructure engineers on deployments, so what you promised in the room is what gets built
* Act as the technical voice of the customer internally, and the credible technical voice of zaimler externally
### Prior Experience
* 5+ years total experience, including 2 to 3 years in a hands-on technical or data role before moving into a customer-facing one. You've built something, not just presented about it
* Enterprise B2B software background; you understand long cycles, procurement, security review, and multi-stakeholder buying
* Track record converting technical proofs of value into production commitments
* Real fluency in the modern data stack: warehouses, pipelines, and how enterprises actually store and govern data
* Working knowledge of how LLM and agentic systems are deployed in production, and honest judgment about what they can and can't do today
* The credibility to hold a room of senior engineers. You can be challenged on architecture and push back without losing them
* Strong read on room dynamics: who holds budget, who holds veto, and who becomes your champion
* Comfortable with ambiguity, and with being the only zaimler person on site
### Nice to Haves
* You've done this at a field-heavy data or AI company
* Experience with knowledge graphs, semantic layers, ontologies, or entity resolution
* Deployments into regulated or air-gapped environments (financial services, insurance, telco, public sector)
* Enough Python or SQL to prototype in front of a customer rather than promising to follow up
* Prior startup or zero-to-one experience where you helped define the motion, not just execute it
* Multilingual, or experience selling across multiple European markets
### Why Join zaimler
* **You'd be early.** Real enterprise deployments already running, no pre-sales org to slot into, no playbook to inherit. How zaimler runs a technical evaluation in EMEA will mostly be how you decide to do it.
* **The problem is genuinely unsolved.** Most of enterprise AI right now is a wrapper. We're building the layer underneath. You'll be explaining something hard to people who will know if you're bluffing.
* **You're building the region, not joining it.** You'll be first on the ground in Europe, and the field motion you establish is the one the team we hire after you will inherit.
* **Close to the people building it.** What you hear in the room goes straight to a founding team still writing the roadmap, not into a request queue.
* **Small enough that you move the number.** You'll be able to point at specific accounts and know they went our way because of you.
We value builders over résumés. If this role excites you but you don't check every box, we still want to hear from you. zaimler is an equal opportunity employer.

Zero100 is a membership-based intelligence company that connects, informs, and inspires the world's most influential C-Level Operations & Supply Chain Officers - and their teams - to unlock the true potential of the AI and Digital Revolution.
Our members use Zero100's our research, advisory services, data, and peer community, to sharpen strategy, challenge assumptions, and accelerate progress on their most important transformation priorities from AI adoption and digitization to resilience and decarbonization.
With a rapidly expanding headquarters in central London, Zero100's members include Nike, Walmart, Unilever, Pfizer, Google, Honeywell, and General Motors.
Recent recognition:

* The Sunday Times 100 (#43), 2025

**What you will do:**
Note that this is a primarily office-based role (~4 days per week).
We are hiring a London-based Senior Analyst, Data & Insights to deliver high-quality, evidence-based analysis that helps the world's top operations and supply chain leaders make better decisions. Your work will directly inform the research, presentations, and advisory services we deliver to our members, translating complex datasets into clear, decision-oriented narratives for C-suite audiences.
We're looking for someone with strong analytical fundamentals who has developed practical working habits with AI tools and understands where they genuinely improve analytical workflows - and where they don't. You should know what good analysis looks like well enough to recognize when AI-generated output is useful, when it needs refinement or validation, and when it shouldn't be relied upon. We're looking for someone who sees these tools as part of a rigorous analytical workflow, not a substitute for structured thinking, sound judgment, or domain understanding.
The right candidate has experience translating data into insights for senior or executive stakeholders, not just building dashboards, but crafting narratives that drive decisions. A consulting-like mindset (comfort with ambiguity, structured thinking, ability to work across diverse problem spaces) is important. You're a strong collaborator who can partner effectively with researchers, understand what customers need, and deliver work that improves customer workflows. As you grow into the role, there will be meaningful opportunity to shape what we investigate, bring forward original insights, and engage directly with customers.
Beyond the day job, we are looking for candidates who share our enthusiasm about the potential for Zero100 to have a positive impact on the supply chain profession and (more broadly) the planet.
**Responsibilities:**
* Deliver data analysis in partnership with the Research team, producing visualizations and data points that feed into customer-facing deliverables (slides, reports, presentations).
* Transform complex datasets into clear, insight-driven narratives tailored for executive audiences.
* Scope data needs for new analyses, partnering with data engineering on pipeline work and leading on transformation, analysis, visualization, and storytelling.
* Ensure quality and integrity of all insights delivered, maintaining a high bar for accuracy and clarity.
* Synthesize across structured and unstructured sources - survey data, executive interview transcripts, operational datasets, and qualitative research notes - to develop insights that wouldn't surface from any single source alone.
* Leverage AI tools (including our internal LLM) to accelerate analysis, explore data, and push the boundaries of how insights are generated.
* Collaborate closely with research, design, and customer-facing teams to understand stakeholder needs and deliver work that exceeds expectations.
* Over time, identify opportunities to proactively surface new insights, propose new lines of inquiry, and contribute to the evolution of our data products.
## Requirements
**Requirements:**
* 5-7 years of experience in data analysis, insights, or a related field, with demonstrated ability to translate data into narratives for senior/executive audiences.
* Strong analytical fundamentals: SQL required, Python preferred, comfort working in environments like Databricks.
* Experience producing data visualizations and charts (Excel/Google Sheets, or directly from analytical tools) with an eye for clarity and storytelling, not just aesthetics.
* Working fluency with AI-assisted analysis and workflow tools. You understand where these tools genuinely improve analytical work, where they fall short, and how to use them to enhance (not replace) rigorous thinking and judgment.
* Structured thinking and comfort with ambiguity. You can take an ambiguous business question, determine what information matters, structure an analytical approach, and translate complex or incomplete inputs into a clear, defensible point of view. You are comfortable navigating uncertainty, forming hypotheses, and iterating toward an answer without needing perfectly defined requirements from the outset.
* Strong collaboration skills. You work well embedded within a research team and can navigate a matrixed, geographically distributed organization.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Familiarity with operations or supply chain is a plus, but curiosity and fast learning matter more.
